findings.title: Hostile embedded-resource failures bypass the required Prepared Scan 503 mapping during DI activation
evidence: contracts/prepared-scan-initiation.md:90 requires missing, duplicate, invalid or mismatched Prepared Pass 1 authority to map to bounded HTTP 503 before fresh authorization or store access; tasks.md:156 requires those hostile authorities to fail HTTP 503.

EmbeddedPreparedPass1ContractIdentitySource.cs:19-38 constructs the scoped production service and eagerly calls GetCurrent; missing, duplicate, empty, invalid-UTF8 and schema-inconsistent resource cases therefore throw from service construction.

Program.cs:365-367 registers that implementation as the scoped IPreparedPass1ContractIdentitySource required to construct PreparedScanInitiationCoordinator, while PreparedScanEndpoints.cs:26 injects the coordinator as a handler parameter. Service activation necessarily precedes the coordinator method's try/catch around GetCurrent.

PreparedPass1ContractIdentitySourceTests.cs:102-131 asserts only that hostile-resource construction throws. PreparedScanInitiationCoordinatorTests.cs:150-205 proves bounded Unavailable only with a proxy whose GetCurrent throws after the coordinator already exists. PreparedScanInitiationApiTests has no hostile embedded-resource public 503 vector.
findings.impact: The path remains fail-closed with respect to initiation writes because handler activation fails before the endpoint body, but the API returns an unhandled activation failure/ordinary 500 path instead of the accepted sanitized 503 ProblemDetails contract. The executable evidence therefore still does not prove the complete T025 public behavior for packaging/resource failures.
findings.remediation: Return to the T025 test-first owner. Add a public WebApplicationFactory endpoint vector for missing, duplicate, invalid-UTF8 and schema-inconsistent embedded authority that observes HTTP 503 with the bounded problem code and zero runtime, fresh-authorization, store and preparation calls. Observe the current activation failure as RED. Then make the smallest correction that lets the coordinator own GetCurrent failure mapping, for example defer resource validation from service construction to GetCurrent while retaining strict validation and the sole Agents-owned source. Rerun the 29-case matrix, the public initiation/API boundary, T029/T030 regression, convergence and a fresh quality review.

boundary_assessment.security: Initial visibility, fresh pre-store authorization and pre-publication authorization remain distinct; denied scope is missing-equivalent and no hostile identity reaches durable creation. The defect is bounded failure semantics and availability, not an observed disclosure or write-before-authorization issue.
boundary_assessment.transactions_and_replay: Initiation and publication transactions execute inside EF execution strategies, use bounded isolation/advisory serialization, canonicalize PostgreSQL instants, clear tracking on failure, and close before external Git/CodeGraph/JDT-LS/XML work. boundary_assessment.architecture: Core remains dependency-free, Agents owns the embedded prompt authority, Infrastructure owns EF/transactions, Web owns Identity/orchestration, and the rechecker uses materialized specific Core repositories without EF/DbContext access. QR-PSI-002 is an integration-order defect at the Agents-to-Web DI seam.

summary: REVISE with one Medium correctness/public-contract finding. QR-PSI-001 is closed by executable hostile identity tests, and the remaining Prepared Scan initiation design, authorization ordering, replay/transaction behavior, prepared-v2 publication, composition and prohibited-scope guards are coherent. However the production embedded authority validates eagerly in its scoped constructor, so hostile resource failures occur during DI activation before the coordinator can map GetCurrent failures to the required bounded HTTP 503. Return only to the T025 identity/composition TDD slice; keep T034-T045/run-03 closed.
